alerts.reason: Citrix's reported revenue growth slowed from 4.68% in September to -0.02% in December. Product and license revenue fell 23.8% in 2020 (A). Subscription growth supports a March quarter above -5%, but $223.5 million of additional subscription revenue was deferred (B, C). I forecast that by the June quarter, recognized subscription revenue will fall short of offsetting license declines by enough for total revenue to fall at least 5% year over year.

Take-Two's December revenue fell 7.44% year over year, but several releases that drove the $73.9 million bookings decline had September–November 2019 launch dates (B). Those launch comparisons pass by March, supporting a recovery above -5%. For April–June, I forecast a fresh decline of at least 5% as revenue is compared with a quarter that benefited from lockdown-driven player engagement (C).

Fastenal's 6.35% December sales growth supports a March quarter above -5%. Pandemic PPE unit sales drove most of 2020's sales increase, while masks were already oversupplied in the second half and pricing had little effect on annual sales (A–D). I forecast that lapping the initial PPE buying in April–June will push consolidated net sales down at least 5% year over year.
